question.problem:
Suppose $T:V\to W$ is a linear map and $B=\{{b}_{1},{b}_{2}\}$ and $C=\{{c}_{1},{c}_{2},{c}_{3}\}$ are the bases of the vector spaces $V$ and $W$, respectively. Find the matrix $[T]_{B|C}$ of the map $T$ relative to these bases, if 

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=6{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3}\,$ and $\,T({b}_{2})=-5{c}_{2}+9{c}_{3}-4{c}_{1}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, we write the images of vectors in $B$ relative to the basis $C:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}T({b}_{1})=6{c}_{1}-{c}_{2}-7{c}_{3} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{1})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ -1 \\ -7\end{aligned}] \\ T({b}_{2})=-5{c}_{2}+9{c}_{3}-4{c}_{1} & \,⟹\,[T({b}_{2})]_{C}=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -5 \\ 9\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, $[T]_{B|C}$ is the matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and  $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $C:$

$$
[T]_{B|C}=[\begin{aligned}6 & -4 \\ -1 & -5 \\ -7 & 9\end{aligned}]
$$
